Hi, thanks for your patience on this one.

Your Shop···· (Magic Miner 40T plus the Power Kit) is paid and hasn't shipped yet. It was due October 15 and the units aren't on the shelf in Chattanooga yet, so it missed that. I'm sorry for the wait. The current date is November 14, and the Power Kit ships in the same box.

You can follow that shipment on its way to us here: https://heliumdeploy.com/pages/shipment-status

Tracking goes to (email hidden) automatically, worth whitelisting us so it doesn't land in spam.

I hear you, and I'm sorry. The October 15 date passed and the units still aren't built, so I understand why you've had enough.

A cancellation on this one isn't something I can complete myself, so I've put your request in front of the team with the order number and what you've asked for. They're offline right now and pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer comes to (email hidden), so you don't need to wait here.

I won't promise you an amount or a date I don't control.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: Georges approved a FULL refund ($835.49) on Shop····: cancel the order with the money back to the original payment. Run the order-swap skill: approved_refund.py check --email <the order's email> --order Shop····, then approved_refund.py refund --email <same> --order Shop···· --confirmed. Only when it reports refunded: true, tell the customer it is done, the amount, and that it goes back to their original payment method, usually 3 to 5 business days to show. If it refuses or reports problems, do not say it is done: flag it and tell the customer the team will confirm the refund shortly.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
